overall_summary: Bitcoin is under clear near-term pressure from large ETF outflows, heavy exchange inflows, and long liquidations, pointing to distribution rather than a finished washout. Sticky inflation, hotter prices, and rising oil add macro headwinds ahead of a likely FOMC hold, while Middle East and Iran risks keep risk appetite capped. Structural ETF progress is a longer-term positive but does not offset today’s defensive flow and macro tone for crypto.
key_points: Large BTC ETF outflows and exchange inflows
Long liquidations as Bitcoin slips under 81K
Sticky inflation and oil surge before FOMC
Elevated Iran and Middle East geopolitical risk

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Post $636M Outflow, Largest Since June
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about six hundred thirty-five to six hundred thirty-six million dollars in net outflows on Thursday, the biggest single day since June. BlackRock's IBIT and Fidelity's FBTC led the redemptions, wiping out most of a recent three-day inflow streak and pushing October flows back into the red. Bitcoin slipped toward the eighty to eighty-one thousand dollar zone as the selling hit. Traders should watch whether outflows continue into the Fed meeting next week, because sustained institutional exits remove a key bid.
items.impact: Adds near-term selling pressure and weakens the institutional demand narrative

items.title: Bitcoin Slips Under $81K With Heavy Long Liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin traded down around the eighty to eighty-one thousand five hundred dollar area, testing key support and printing a daily close below its fifty-day moving average for the first time in months. CoinGlass and other trackers showed three hundred to five hundred million dollars in liquidations over twenty-four hour windows, with longs making up the vast majority. The move came alongside a Nasdaq sell-off, elevated oil prices, and caution ahead of the Fed decision. For traders this is a risk-off tape that can cascade if eighty thousand fails to hold.
items.impact: Heightens downside volatility risk if support breaks

items.title: Record $2.6B Bitcoin Inflow to Exchanges Since April
items.summary: On-chain data showed roughly thirty-two thousand three hundred eighty Bitcoin, worth about two point six billion dollars, flowing into exchanges in a single day. That marks the largest such inflow since April. Large exchange deposits often precede selling, though they do not guarantee immediate dumps. Traders watching order books and spot selling should treat this as elevated supply risk while price sits near support.
items.impact: Raises potential near-term sell-side pressure on Bitcoin

items.title: Arthur Hayes Closes Maelstrom Book, Sells $22M Tokens
items.summary: BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes said he dumped Maelstrom's entire directional trading book, taking profits on Ethereum, Ethena, Uniswap and other tokens totaling around twenty-two million dollars. On-chain trackers confirmed large transfers including thousands of ETH. He cited dicey macro and geopolitical conditions and said he will sit on the sidelines waiting for an all-clear. This is a high-profile risk-off signal from a closely followed trader that can weigh on sentiment, especially for ETH and alts.
items.impact: Negative sentiment hit for ETH and broader risk appetite

items.title: Franklin Templeton Clears Nasdaq for Stock-Bitcoin ETFs
items.summary: Franklin Templeton completed Form 8-A registration for two new Nasdaq-listed ETFs that start with roughly ninety-five percent U.S. stocks and five percent Bitcoin exposure. Dividends from the equity sleeve get reinvested into Bitcoin via a DRIP-style mechanism, with tickers FBEQ and FIBT and expected trading around October twenty-seven. Fees are low at zero point zero nine and zero point one nine percent. This expands mainstream product access and creates a structural drip of equity dividends into Bitcoin demand over time.
items.impact: Positive longer-term structural demand and product innovation signal

items.title: BlackRock ETF Wallets Move $356M BTC and ETH to Coinbase
items.summary: Wallets linked to BlackRock ETFs transferred about three thousand two hundred fifteen Bitcoin worth two hundred sixty-two million dollars plus nearly thirty-nine thousand Ether worth ninety-three million to Coinbase Prime in a short window. The moves align with the prior day's heavy ETF outflows and are widely read as redemption settlement rather than discretionary dumping. Still, large visible transfers to an exchange desk keep traders on alert for related selling. Watch actual ETF flow prints more than the wallet headlines for the real signal.
items.impact: Operational echo of redemptions; limited fresh directional catalyst

items.title: Oil Surges to Multi-Month Highs on Middle East Risks
items.summary: Brent crude settled around one hundred sixteen dollars seventy-two cents and WTI above one hundred three dollars on Friday, the highest closes in months, after Houthi attacks on Saudi sites and rising US-Iran tensions. This energy shock is already feeding into higher gasoline prices and inflation expectations. Crypto traders should watch closely because sticky energy inflation raises the odds the Fed stays higher for longer, pressuring risk assets including Bitcoin.
items.impact: Supports higher rates and weighs on risk appetite

items.title: US Flash PMI Shows Strong Growth but Hottest Prices in Years
items.summary: October flash composite PMI came in at fifty-seven point six, still signaling robust expansion near multi-year highs, with manufacturing at fifty-six and services near fifty-eight. Hiring accelerated but selling prices rose at the sharpest pace since twenty twenty-two. This combination of solid activity and reaccelerating price pressures gives the Fed little room to ease and keeps December hike odds alive heading into next week's meeting.

items.title: Treasury Yields Plunge Then Stabilize Near Five Percent
items.summary: The ten-year yield crashed nearly nineteen basis points on Thursday in its biggest drop since the twenty twenty-three banking scare on AI funding fears and risk-off flows, then edged back toward five percent on Friday. Two-year yields also fell sharply before rebounding. Markets have essentially priced out an October Fed hike while still seeing solid chances of a December move, leaving bonds sensitive to any oil or inflation surprises.
items.impact: Lower yields temporarily support risk assets but volatility high

items.title: Consumer Sentiment Near Record Lows, Inflation Expectations Rise
items.summary: University of Michigan final October sentiment held at forty-eight, the second-lowest reading on record and only slightly above May's trough, though better than the preliminary print. One-year inflation expectations ticked up to four point seven percent and longer-term views also rose. Weak confidence amid higher energy costs could eventually slow spending, but elevated inflation expectations keep the Fed on guard.
items.impact: Soft demand signal offset by sticky inflation views

items.title: Jobless Claims Stay Extremely Low at 194,000
items.summary: Initial jobless claims fell six thousand to one hundred ninety-four thousand for the week ending October seventeenth, beating expectations and keeping the four-week average near one hundred ninety-eight thousand. The labor market remains in a low-hire low-fire mode with no sign of cracking. Resilient claims data support the case for solid growth but also reduce any urgency for the Fed to cut or pause aggressively.
items.impact: Confirms labor resilience, little pressure for easing

items.title: FOMC Next Week Expected to Hold Rates Amid Sticky Inflation
items.summary: The Fed meets October twenty-seven and twenty-eight with markets pricing roughly a ninety percent chance of no change to the three point seven five to four percent range. Focus will be on Chair Warsh's press conference for clues on December and the reaction to oil-driven inflation. No new projections are due, so language on energy prices and the path of rates will move yields, the dollar, and crypto.
items.impact: Hold base case; guidance is the real catalyst

items.title: US Intel: Iran Advanced Plots to Kill Americans; Trump Teases Strikes
items.summary: A US intelligence memo to Secretary Rubio warns that Iranian lethal plots against American personnel have reached advanced stages in the Middle East and elsewhere, prompting embassy staff reductions and heightened alerts. President Trump separately said the US may launch another little Epic Fury operation against Iran if no deal is reached, with officials noting post-midterm strike plans. Traders should watch this closely because any renewed kinetic action risks a sharp oil spike and broad risk-off move that hits Bitcoin and equities hard.
items.impact: Heightened Middle East escalation premium lifts oil and pressures risk assets

items.title: Melania Trump Brokers Localized Oleshky Ceasefire in Ukraine
items.summary: The White House announced that First Lady Melania Trump secured a temporary localized ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the occupied city of Oleshky to allow humanitarian aid and civilian evacuations starting late October. Both sides confirmed forces will pause fire around October 27 for the operation. For markets this is a small positive de-escalation signal amid broader peace-talk efforts, though it does not end the wider war or immediately change energy flows.
items.impact: Minor positive for risk sentiment if it builds momentum toward wider talks

items.title: Netanyahu Orders Full West Bank Lockdown After Hebron Attack
items.summary: After two Israeli soldiers were killed near Hebron, Prime Minister Netanyahu ordered a complete lockdown of the West Bank, house-to-house operations, and demolitions just days before Israeli elections. Israeli forces have already raided multiple towns and detained dozens. This raises short-term regional tension and could spill into broader Middle East risk, keeping oil supported and risk assets cautious ahead of the vote.
items.impact: Adds another layer of Middle East instability supporting energy prices

items.title: First Russian Diesel Tanker Heads to US Under Trump-Putin Deal
items.summary: Ship-tracking data shows a tanker loaded with 40,000 tons of Russian ultra-low-sulfur diesel left Primorsk bound for New York, the first such US-bound cargo under the recent Trump-Putin energy arrangement. The Kremlin confirmed the initial shipment with more to follow after Washington eased sanctions. This is a direct attempt to ease US diesel prices before the midterms and could modestly relieve energy cost pressure if volumes scale.
items.impact: Potential relief for elevated diesel prices supports risk assets and growth

items.title: Ukraine Says Starlink Limits Still in Place Despite Trump Claims
items.summary: Ukrainian officials including President Zelenskyy stated that speed restrictions on Starshield and Starlink remain active, hampering drone operations, even after President Trump said Elon Musk had restored access following a call. The throttling has been linked to pressure over Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure. Continued limits weaken Ukraine’s battlefield edge and keep the conflict’s energy and geopolitical uncertainty elevated for markets.
items.impact: Prolongs Ukraine war friction without immediate directional catalyst

items.title: Brazil Heads into Tight Presidential Runoff Sunday
items.summary: Brazilians vote Sunday in a razor-close presidential runoff between incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro, son of the former president. Polls show the race essentially tied, with implications for Latin America’s largest economy, commodity policy, and relations with the US under Trump. A shift could move agricultural and energy markets and influence broader emerging-market risk appetite.
items.impact: Election outcome may drive LatAm FX, equities and commodity volatility
